# Wave15 validation donor corpus

The unmodified Python donor files and release inputs are frozen from commit
`810b0f9fef7bc444f88f43182c7278fe7039c236`. `provenance.json` pins every
byte of the donor, input corpus and source evidence, the scenario definitions,
and the generated oracle. The Python 3.12 generator uses only these files,
injects the frozen route catalogue and `INTERNAL` constant, and executes each
case in an isolated temporary directory. It never reads live release data,
registries, caches or production Python. The KFP import is an unused stub; KFP
is not implemented or selected by this scope. The variable sandbox prefix in a
file-not-found message is replaced with `<sandbox>`; the rest of each donor
diagnostic is compared exactly.

The bill DOCX is the original 1,936,694-byte file, SHA256
`378042f3c6f05aad760099f3b5ccceaf597fd287b28242fe89b99d2a981fc174`.
Separate cases exercise its presence, absence and hash mismatch. The missing
case preserves the donor warning; no placeholder stands in for an original.

`evidence/programme-pdf.json` is a byte-pinned copy of the independently
captured PDF reader evidence in the earlier programme corpus, which records
source hashes and extraction provenance. `evidence/parliament.json` is the
frozen Parliament activity captured in the earlier law corpus. Changed and
repaired scenarios derive programme page 5 from the captured PDF cells and the
adoption date from the independently recorded parliamentary activity. Another
pair changes and restores the measures page, deriving page 215 from page breaks
and the measure text in the pinned DOCX. These are evidence-backed preimages,
not results invented by the TypeScript builder. A donor parity PASS only means
that TypeScript agrees with the donor: for example, the donor checks that the
measures page is an integer, not that it equals the actual source page. Captured
PDF cells are extraction evidence, not the original programme PDF bytes.

`mutations/` contains the final serialized changed inputs generated by Python.
They retain numeric token kinds for the TypeScript tests; regeneration verifies
their exact file set and bytes. Cases include mixed integer/float accumulation,
non-finite tokens, absent documents and fields, source and metadata changes,
rounding boundaries, sparse values, whitespace, tree links, law reconciliation
and the programme index. They do not claim exhaustive coverage of all possible
inputs. No live release is compared with this frozen oracle in CI.

Run with Python 3.12:

```sh
python packages/ingest/test/fixtures/validate15/generate_oracle.py --check
```

To intentionally regenerate, omit `--check` and review the scenario, oracle and
provenance changes together. The scoped CLI requires explicit `--root` or
`--live`; `--live` is a local diagnostic, separate from this proof. Production
continues to use Python, and BUDGET2027 and the other listed unported groups
remain outside the TypeScript scope.

The acceptance additions preserve the original 206 scenario definitions and all 212 observations byte-semantically. There are now 442 definitions yielding 448 donor observations. The additions cover absent/null/integer/float/bool offsets, list/slice errors, empty memo containers, boolean-number equality, required subscription callsites, explicit invalid arithmetic/sequence operands, lazy evaluation and first-error order, blank cells and exact diagnostic representations. Nested integer-like mapping keys retain their source order alongside raw float kinds. Composite cases check short-circuit behavior rather than imposing an eager validation pass. All 64 original input pins and the frozen donor files remain unchanged; only the appended scenarios, mutations and oracle digests change.
